New: a merge gate, live review progress and replies on your comments in the pull request review window.

What's new

- Merge gate: every review ends in Ready to merge, Not ready or Needs your look, with the reasons listed. Approve follows the gate; Approve anyway stays available behind a confirm.
- Live progress: while a review runs, the window shows the steps, each reviewer as waiting, running or done, how many files are checked, and what is happening now. The notch chip shows the elapsed time and reviewers done.
- Cards come only from the checked report, so every card traces to a finding that was re-checked in the code.
- "Was already there": a bug that was in the code before the pull request, on a line it touches, gets its own card and never blocks on its own. Bugs on lines the pull request does not touch go to a Follow-ups list.
- Replies: the window reads replies on comments you posted and marks them seen when you leave the pull request.
- Follow-up reviews read other people's open comments and the gate, split big diffs, and keep one result per head commit.
- Resolve all fixed: pick the fixed threads and resolve them in one step, behind one confirm.
- Each run is kept; cards are rebuilt from the latest one. A run stopped by the time limit is recorded as stopped.
- Lessons: after a review the app can propose lessons from what was missed or wrongly raised. Each one is added to the review skill only when you approve it.
- PRs list: status badge, two-line titles, five rows, sorted by what needs you, hover actions and a manual refresh.
- A full review may now run for 90 minutes (was 30), for large pull requests.

Fixed

- Tool calls are counted when only the post event arrives.
- "Need you" counts only what waits on you.

Limits

- The gate relies on the pipeline result; the app runs no tests itself. Where the pipeline proves nothing the result is Needs your look.
- The live "now" line names the kind of step, not the file it is on, and there is no cost so far while a review runs.
- A full review of a large pull request takes 20 to 30 minutes.
- Posting, Approve, Request changes, Resolve and tasks need the Bitbucket API token with write access to pull requests (Setup → Pull requests).

Install or upgrade:

    brew install --cask ankeshshankar/tap/ai-notch
    brew upgrade --cask ai-notch

After upgrading, the app is signed ad hoc, so macOS forgets Microphone, Input Monitoring and Accessibility: remove AI Notch from each list in System Settings → Privacy & Security, add it again, then quit and reopen the app.

First open: the app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so macOS blocks it once. Open AI Notch, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. If Set Up then reports the helper is blocked, run the command it shows:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AINotch.app

Requires macOS 15 or later (dictation: macOS 26).
